title: Rational-base Lambert series: primitive local obstructions and additive repair

concepts.label: row-content neutrality
concepts.note: Scalar content multiplies the linear-form error, exterior determinant, and absolute determinant height by the same factors.

concepts.label: opposite endpoint residues at 3/2
concepts.note: Homogeneous specialization modulo 3 sees the constant endpoint, while modulo 2 it sees the top endpoint.

concepts.label: binary four-jet kernel
concepts.note: A pigeonhole collision among binary selectors yields a signed relation cancelling two endpoint jets in each of two coefficient sequences.

concepts.label: external 7/2 height route
concepts.note: The elementary inequality side of the Bundschuh–Väänänen criterion at base 7/2, with the analytic irrationality theorem remaining external.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED BARRIER: multiplying two integer coefficient rows by scalar contents multiplies their linear-form errors rowwise and multiplies both their exterior determinant and its absolute height by exactly the product of the two contents; the same product divides the scaled determinant, so content alone creates no net local-to-Archimedean gain.
statement_nodes.engine: exact scalar factorization of errors and exterior determinants
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made; the problem note presents this as a checked exclusion for one linear-form mechanism.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This removes scalar row content as a source of gain. It does not construct primitive Padé rows, prove a nonzero determinant, estimate a remainder, or settle irrationality at 3/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED: homogeneous evaluation of an integral polynomial at (3,2) is congruent modulo 3 to its constant coefficient times 2^W and modulo 2 to its top coefficient times 3^W; a unit constant endpoint therefore excludes divisibility by 3, and a unit top endpoint excludes divisibility by 2.
statement_nodes.engine: endpoint survival under homogeneous specialization modulo the two local primes
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made; these elementary congruences are recorded because they expose the exact primitive obstruction.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The result concerns endpoint residues of a fixed polynomial. It does not show that a useful Padé family has the required unit endpoints.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED BARRIER: if one coefficient polynomial has a unit top endpoint, the other has a unit constant endpoint, and an integer divides both homogeneous evaluations at (3,2), then that common multiplier is divisible by neither 2 nor 3.
statement_nodes.engine: opposite endpoint residue exclusions combined on one coefficient pair
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made; the paper uses this together with row-content neutrality to rule out multiplicative local gain.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem is conditional on the unit endpoints and only excludes a common multiplier. It does not exclude additive cancellations or every primitive local-divisibility mechanism.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL CONSTRUCTION: at positive bottom depth, once the number of coefficient pairs reaches the explicit threshold n >= 4R+2S, two distinct binary selectors have the same four endpoint jets; subtracting them gives a nonzero {-1,0,1}-valued selector relation cancelling both bottom and top jets in both sequences.
open_antecedents: A growing-rank family whose resulting signed combination has a nonzero polynomial pair and a nonzero sufficiently small analytic remainder
statement_nodes.engine: finite four-jet signature count and pigeonhole collision among binary selectors
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: No priority or novelty claim is made. The collision is the additive repair proposed after the multiplicative no-go.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem constructs a selector relation only. It does not prove that the combined polynomial pair or analytic remainder is nonzero, nor that the remainder decays fast enough for irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CONDITIONAL BARRIER: under the source scalar-cone inequality used by the Zudilin-style construction, the corresponding product-formula margin at base 3/2 is strictly negative.
open_antecedents: The source scalar-cone inequality assumed by the theorem
statement_nodes.engine: exact specialization of the source height parameters at numerator 3 and denominator 2
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The inequality is presented as a checked consequence of an assumed source input, not as a new irrationality theorem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The source inequality is an explicit hypothesis. A negative scalar margin excludes that parameter lane; it does not exclude higher-rank additive kernels.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED ARITHMETIC INPUT: base 7/2 satisfies the explicit power, logarithmic, pi, margin, and final Archimedean height inequalities required by the cited Bundschuh–Väänänen criterion.
open_antecedents: The external Bundschuh–Väänänen analytic irrationality theorem is cited rather than formalized
statement_nodes.engine: kernel-checked elementary numerical and logarithmic inequalities at 7/2
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The irrationality criterion is attributed to Bundschuh and Väänänen (1994); only its elementary arithmetic height side is formalized here.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This node does not formalize or reprove the external analytic theorem and says nothing about the resistant base 3/2.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The common-multiplier exclusion applies the separate modulo-2 and modulo-3 endpoint unit obstructions to the two entries of one coefficient pair.
Endpoint residues exclude a common specialized multiplier, while row-content neutrality separately excludes scalar content as net local gain.
After the multiplicative route is excluded under unit endpoints, the four-jet collision supplies an additive cancellation mechanism whose remaining analytic obligations are explicit.
The scalar-cone margin and endpoint/common-multiplier obstruction are independent checked failures of scalar multiplicative variants at 3/2.
The cited external height criterion succeeds arithmetically at 7/2, while the checked scalar-cone product-formula margin is negative at the resistant base 3/2.
